spec.title: Morning routine — the human side of WAL

p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The five-minute human ritual at the start of each day: read the WAL, reconcile it with your own memory, and only then let an agent session begin.

p.WAL-IS-A-TWO-SIDED-PROTOCOL: The WAL is a two-sided protocol — the agent writes it at the end of each session, the human reads it at the start of each day.

p.WITHOUT-THE-MORNING-READ-THE-WAL-ROTS: Without the morning read, the WAL rots: the agent's claim that "all tests pass" drifts from your memory that the timeout test was flaky yesterday.

p.before-coding-lead: Before opening any code, before starting any agent session:

item.STEP-COMPARE-AGAINST-WHAT-YOU-REMEMBER: Compare what it says against what you remember.

p.HEAD-WINS-EDIT-THE-WAL-TO-MATCH-MEMORY: If the WAL and your memory disagree, **head wins** — edit the WAL to match what you remember, *then* start the session.

p.why-head-wins: Head wins because persistent human memory is the one authoritative channel the agent cannot reach directly.

p.a-flaky-test-example: If the WAL says "all tests pass" and you remember the timeout test is flaky, the WAL is wrong: fix it before the next agent session reads and trusts it.

p.top-of-the-conflict-hierarchy: (This is the top of the conflict hierarchy — Human > Spec > Tests > Code > WAL.)

skim.title: Fast skim: wal-status

p.the-daily-read-has-a-fast-form: The daily read has a fast form.

p.FLOW-SHIPS-A-WAL-STATUS-SKILL: This flow ships a `wal-status` skill: install it into your agent and ask for a WAL status at session start.

p.SKILL-ANSWERS-IN-AT-MOST-TEN-LINES: It reads `spec/WAL.md` end to end and answers in at most ten lines — one line of phase and status, up to three attention bullets, one line of next step — warning first when the WAL is older than 24 hours.

p.equivalent-prompt-lead: For an agent without skill support, paste the equivalent prompt into your project's agent instructions:

skim.fence: ## /wal-status Read spec/WAL.md end to end. Emit in ≤ 10 lines: - one line: current phase and status - up to three bullets: what needs attention (blockers, risks) - one line: next priority step If the WAL `_Updated:` line is older than 24 hours, warn first.

p.the-summary-is-a-quick-daily-read: The ten-line summary is a quick daily read.

p.THE-SKIM-DOES-NOT-REPLACE-THE-WEEKLY-RE-: It does not replace the end-of-week full re-read — the same way a `top` command does not replace looking at dashboards.

p.cold-start-situations: Coming back after a machine switch or a long gap, or arriving at a repository that is not yours?

p.READ-CONTINUE-FIRST-THEN-THE-WAL: Read `CONTINUE.md` at the repository root first — it carries the tour, the commands, the map — then `spec/WAL.md`, which is canonical wherever the two diverge.

p.RE-READ-KEY-SPEC-DOCUMENTS-WEEKLY: Once a week, re-read the key spec documents end-to-end. Watch for:

item.WATCH-FOR-INTERNAL-CONTRADICTIONS: Internal contradictions (§2 says one thing, §5 says another).

item.WATCH-FOR-STALE-REVIEW-MARKERS: REVIEW markers older than your configured threshold.

p.A-SCHEDULED-RE-READ-IS-THE-GARBAGE-COLLE: A scheduled re-read is the garbage collector for the spec corpus.

stale.title: If the WAL is clearly stale

p.A-STALE-DATE-LINE-MEANS-THE-LAST-SESSION: If you come back after a week and the WAL's `_Updated:` line is from last Tuesday, the previous session clearly did not close cleanly. Your move:

item.STALE-STEP-DO-NOT-START-A-SESSION-YET: Do NOT start a new agent session yet.

item.STALE-STEP-RECONSTRUCT-FROM-GIT: Look at `git log` and `git diff` for the interval. Reconstruct what actually happened.

item.STALE-STEP-REWRITE-THE-WAL-BY-HAND: Rewrite the WAL yourself to reflect the true current state.

p.THE-HUMAN-IS-THE-BACKUP-FOR-THE-WAL: The human is the backup for the WAL.

p.where-the-human-is-irreplaceable: This is one of the situations where the human is irreplaceable in the system, and where ten minutes of manual reconciliation prevents hours of agent confusion.

item.NEVER-START-ON-A-WAL-YOU-HAVE-NOT-READ-T: Never start an agent session on a WAL you have not read today.

item.NEVER-FIX-A-STALE-WAL-FROM-MEMORY-ALONE: Never "fix" a stale WAL from memory alone — reconstruct from `git log` and `git diff` first; memory is reconstructive, not archival.

item.NEVER-LET-THE-SKIM-REPLACE-THE-WEEKLY-RE: Never let the skim replace the weekly full re-read.

item.NEVER-LEAVE-A-KNOWN-DIVERGENCE-FOR-LATER: Never leave a known divergence in place "for later" — the very next session will read and trust it.

item.SUM-READ-THE-WAL-EVERY-MORNING: Read the WAL every morning, end to end, before any session.

item.SUM-HEAD-WINS: Head wins: your memory corrects the WAL, never the other way around.

item.SUM-SKIM-AND-WEEKLY-RE-READ: `wal-status` is the fast skim; the weekly full re-read still happens.

item.SUM-COLD-START-ORDER: Cold start? `CONTINUE.md` first for the tour, the WAL for the truth.

item.SUM-STALE-WAL-PROCEDURE: Stale WAL: reconstruct from git, rewrite by hand, then start.
